summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of HfO2 onto Si using Hf(NMe2)4 as a precursor. The temperature window for ALD was determined based on the thermal decomposition characteristics of Hf(NMe2)4. The deposited HfO2 films showed excellent electrical properties suitable for CMOS devices, with an equivalent-oxide thickness (EOT) of 2.5 nm and a leakage current density of 1.3×10−6 A/cm² at −1 V. The lower leakage current was attributed to the formation of an SiNx interlayer during ALD, which was confirmed by in-situ XPS and residue analysis.
evidence: The temperature window for the ALD of HfO2 was determined based on the thermal decomposition characteristics of Hf(NMe2)4. The growth rate of the HfO2 obtained in the temperature window was ca. 1.2 Å/cycle. The prepared film had electrical properties suitable for use in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) devices, showing an equivalent-oxide thickness (EOT) of 2.5 nm and a leakage current density of 1:3×10−6 A/cm² at −1 V. The leakage current was three orders of magnitude lower than that of SiO2 with the same EOT. The lower current leakage was obtained because N atoms in the Hf(NMe2)4 formed an SiNx interlayer by reaction with the Si substrate during the ALD, as confirmed by in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and by the analysis of residue on the substrate after the decomposition of the Hf precursor.
